newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks optimistic about bottled coffee, earnings.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks optimistic about bottled coffee, earnings.

text.p: Starbucks Corp. President Orin Smith said on Thursday he thought annual revenues from the coffee bar chain's bottled coffee beverage could eventually exceed $1 billion.
The Kent, Wash.-based company is preparing for a national rollout this summer of its bottled Frappuccino in a joint venture with PepsiCo Inc.

Speaking at the company's annual shareholders meeting in Kent, Smith said PepsiCo officials were estimating the beverage could bring in revenues of $400 million to $500 million in its first full year of national distribution.
In the fiscal year ended Sept. 29, 1996, Starbucks reported a profit of $42.1 million, or 54 cents a share, on revenues of $696.5 million.
The Frappuccino product is a 50-50 joint venture between the two companies and any income or losses would be split equally between Starbucks and PepsiCo.
Smith said the product would be available in most major markets in the United States by the end of this year but it would not achieve full national distribution until the end of fiscal 1998.
Smith said he could not predict when the bottled beverage revenues would reach $1 billion.
Starbucks and PepsiCo are investing a total of $50 million on production facilities for their bottled coffee beverages during the next two to three years.
